# CLI reference

<!-- Generated by `helix-loop docs` from the commands themselves. Do not edit by hand. -->

Build a product from a spec with headless coding agents, in a loop you steer.
Every command also answers `--help`.

Commands act on the project around the current folder: the nearest folder up with a `.helix/` folder.
`--root <dir>` or `$HELIX_PROJECT` names another.

## Options for every command

| Option | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--root <dir>` | The project to act on. By default, the nearest folder up from here with a .helix/ folder, or $HELIX_PROJECT. |
| `--json` | Machine-readable output, for commands that list or show something. |
| `-h, --help` | Show help for helix-loop or for one command. |
| `-v, --version` | Show the version. |

## Start a project

### helix-loop init

Start a Helix Loop project in this folder: the .helix/ folder, its config and its repos

```
helix-loop init [options]
```

Asks for the product's name, who steers it, its time zone, the repositories to build and their gate commands, and the agents to use, then writes .helix/: config.yaml, the build prompt, and folders for the spec and the TaskSet.
Each repository is cloned into .helix/repos/<name>, or started empty for the loop to build from scratch.
It offers to install the Helix skill too. Everything it asks has an option, for scripts; --yes takes the defaults.

| Option | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--name <name>` | The product's name (default: this folder's) |
| `--owner <name>` | Who steers the loop and does its human tasks (default: your git name) |
| `--timezone <zone>` | The time zone dates are written in, as America/Chicago (default: this machine's) |
| `--repo <name[=url]>` | A repository to build: its name, and a git URL or path to clone, or nothing to start it empty. Repeat for each. |
| `--gate <command>` | The command that fully checks a repo before a merge (default: pnpm run gate) |
| `--agents <list>` | The agents to build with: claude, codex or both (default: those installed) |
| `--spec <file>` | A spec to start from, copied into .helix/spec/ |
| `--skill <global|project|none>` | Install the Helix skill too, and where |
| `-y, --yes` | Take the defaults instead of asking |

Examples:

```sh
# Answer a few questions and start
helix-loop init
# Start without questions: one repo cloned, one started empty
helix-loop init --name Acme --repo acme-app=git@github.com:acme/app.git --repo acme-site --yes
```

### helix-loop doctor

Check this machine and the project: Node, git, the agents, the config, the repos, the plan

```
helix-loop doctor
```

### helix-loop skill install

Install the Helix skill for Claude Code and Codex, globally or into one project

```
helix-loop skill install [options]
```

The Helix skill teaches Claude Code and Codex to write a Helix Spec and a Helix TaskSet (/helix spec, /helix harden, /helix taskset, /helix validate), offline.
Without options it asks where to install it: globally (~/.claude/skills/helix, ~/.codex/skills/helix) or into one project (<project>/.claude/skills/helix, <project>/.codex/skills/helix), and for which agents.
Installing again updates it in place.

| Option | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--global` | Install it for every project on this machine |
| `--project <dir>` | Install it into this project folder only |
| `--agent <claude|codex|both>` | The agents to install it for (default: those installed here) |
| `--to <dir>` | Install it into exactly this folder instead |

Examples:

```sh
# Ask where, then install
helix-loop skill install
# Install it for Claude Code and Codex, everywhere
helix-loop skill install --global --agent both
# Install it into this project only
helix-loop skill install --project .
```

### helix-loop skill

```
helix-loop skill [options]
```

| Option | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--json` | Machine-readable output, for commands that list or show something. |

### helix-loop skill pack

Build helix-skill.zip, to upload the skill where a folder can't go (claude.ai, a team)

```
helix-loop skill pack [file]
```

| Argument | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `file` | Where to write it (default: ./helix-skill.zip) (optional) |

### helix-loop migrate

Move a control plane from before .helix/ (spec/, plan/, harness/config.yaml, runs/) into .helix/

```
helix-loop migrate [options]
```

For a project that ran Helix Loop from inside it, before the tool stood alone: moves the spec, the TaskSet, the build prompt, the config and Helix's files into .helix/ with git mv, and the loop's runs, repos and worktrees after them (repairing the worktrees' links).
The loop must be stopped. Without --apply it only says what it would do.

| Option | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--apply` | Do it |
| `--name <name>` | The product's name, for the config's new project block |
| `--owner <name>` | Who steers the loop, for the project block |
| `--timezone <zone>` | The time zone, for the project block |
| `--env-prefix <PREFIX>` | The prefix the product's scripts read the loop's variables under (<PREFIX>_GATE_ID) |

## Spec and TaskSet

### helix-loop spec index

Split the spec into sections and index its requirements

```
helix-loop spec index
```

Reads .helix/spec/ (spec.md, or the one other Markdown file there) and writes .helix/spec/sections/ and .helix/spec/index.json.
Builders get only the sections their task cites, so run this after every change to the spec.

### helix-loop spec sections

List the section keys a task can cite, with their sizes

```
helix-loop spec sections [filter] [options]
```

| Argument | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `filter` | Only keys that contain this text (optional) |

| Option | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--json` | Machine-readable output, for commands that list or show something. |

### helix-loop validate

Check the plan: schemas, dependencies, repos, coverage, prompt sizes, state

```
helix-loop validate [options]
```

Runs every check the loop runs before it starts: each task and human task against the schemas, every dependency resolving with no cycles and no task waiting on a later stage, each task's repo in the config, every requirement claimed by a task (or deferred), each task's prompt within its budget, and claim state that makes sense.
Exits 0 when the plan is clean, 1 when it has problems.

| Option | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--json` | Machine-readable output, for commands that list or show something. |

### helix-loop plan render

Write the Implementation Plan, the Human Implementation Plan and the dependency map

```
helix-loop plan render
```

Writes .helix/plan/ImplementationPlan.md (Lane › Epic › Task), HumanImplementationPlan.md (the steps only the owner can do, with start-by dates) and DependencyMap.html, from the plan as it stands.
The app and Helix run this after every plan change; never edit those files by hand.

### helix-loop plan map

Write the dependency map, a self-contained HTML Gantt chart

```
helix-loop plan map
```

Writes .helix/plan/DependencyMap.html: every task and human task against time, the critical path highlighted. It opens in any browser, with no app running; the app's Map is the live version.

### helix-loop taskset

Show the TaskSet: lanes, their epics in order, and how far each has got

```
helix-loop taskset [options]
```

| Option | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--json` | Machine-readable output, for commands that list or show something. |

### helix-loop taskset init

Write taskset.yaml for a plan that has none, one epic per lane and feature

```
helix-loop taskset init
```

For a plan written before TaskSets: writes .helix/plan/taskset.yaml with its stages, both timelines, and one epic per lane and feature, and sets each task's epic.
Rename, split and merge the epics afterwards (keep each task's epic in step), or regroup the plan properly with the Helix skill and `helix-loop taskset import`.

### helix-loop taskset import

Check a TaskSet from the Helix skill and bring it into the plan

```
helix-loop taskset import <path> [options]
```

Takes a TaskSet folder (taskset.yaml, tasks/, human/, or a plan/ folder holding them) or a zip of one.
It is checked against the schemas and its dependency graph, then compared with the running plan: what it adds, what it removes (only tasks nobody has started), and the tasks it keeps as they are because they are merged, running or attempted.
Nothing is written without --apply (one commit) or --dry-run (into the dry run, to watch it with the fake agents first).

| Argument | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `path` | A TaskSet folder or a zip of one |

| Option | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--apply` | Write it into the plan, as one commit |
| `--dry-run` | Write it into a fresh dry run instead, to try it with the fake agents |

Examples:

```sh
# See what the TaskSet would change
helix-loop taskset import ~/Downloads/helix-taskset.zip
# Bring it into the plan
helix-loop taskset import ./taskset --apply
```

## The loop

### helix-loop run

Run the loop: build the plan with the agents until it is done or stopped

```
helix-loop run [options]
```

Runs passes in parallel, up to each agent's slots, the critical path first, never two in one area at once, and merges each pass that passes its repo's gate.
It paces each agent to last its subscription's week, and drops to one agent, or waits, when one reaches a limit.
It runs in the foreground; stop it gracefully with `helix-loop stop` (or Ctrl-C, which stops at once).
Exit codes: 0 every task is done, 10 only work that needs a person is left, 3 stopped, 1 an error.

| Option | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--max-passes <N>` | Stop after N passes |
| `--agents <list>` | The agents to run this time, comma-separated (claude, codex); overrides agents.*.enabled |
| `--dry-run` | Run on a copy of the plan in .helix/runs/dry-run/, with fake agents and throwaway repos |
| `--config-changes <file>` | With --dry-run: a config change set (JSON) applied to the dry run first |
| `--plan-changes <file>` | With --dry-run: plan changes (JSON, as a fix holds them) applied to the dry run first |

Examples:

```sh
# Build until everything is done
helix-loop run
# Run only Codex, for ten passes
helix-loop run --agents codex --max-passes 10
# Watch the loop work a copy of the plan with fake agents
helix-loop run --dry-run
```

### helix-loop stop

Stop the loop gracefully: no new passes, and it exits once the running ones end

```
helix-loop stop
```

### helix-loop pause

Pause new passes; running passes finish, and the loop waits instead of exiting

```
helix-loop pause
```

### helix-loop resume

Let the loop start new passes again

```
helix-loop resume
```

### helix-loop status

One screen: the loop, the passes in flight, the tasks, the agents, the finish

```
helix-loop status [options]
```

| Option | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--json` | Machine-readable output, for commands that list or show something. |

### helix-loop stats

How the build has used each agent: working, gating, limited, idle, and what it cost

```
helix-loop stats
```

### helix-loop metrics

Write a version of the metrics page now

```
helix-loop metrics
```

Writes the metrics page as a new version in .helix/runs/metrics/ (open its index.html): progress and its projection, where the time goes, cost, and what fails.
The loop writes one every metrics_every_passes passes on its own and keeps each as it was.

## Releases

### helix-loop releases

What each repo has merged since its last release, and what waits for approval

```
helix-loop releases [options]
```

| Option | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--json` | Machine-readable output, for commands that list or show something. |

### helix-loop release run

Release a repo's main now, with the loop's holds

```
helix-loop release run <repo>
```

Tags the repo's main as a release now, as the loop's own checkpoints do, and pushes the tag when push is on.
A release is held while the repo waits on a human task (release.hold_until), and one that changes a reviewed path (release.review_paths) waits for `helix-loop release approve`.
Exit codes: 0 released (or nothing new), 10 held until a person acts, 1 an error.

| Argument | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `repo` | The repo to release |

### helix-loop release approve

Tag and push a release held for review, once its diff is read

```
helix-loop release approve <repo> <tag>
```

A release that changes a reviewed path (CI workflows, infrastructure: what runs with production's secrets) waits in .helix/runs/approvals/. `helix-loop releases` lists them with the command that shows the diff; this tags exactly the commit that was reviewed.

| Argument | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `repo` | The repo |
| `tag` | The release tag, as `helix-loop releases` lists it |

## The app

### helix-loop app

Open Helix Loop, the control room: Home, the Map, Live, Helix, the metrics, Settings

```
helix-loop app [options]
```

Serves the app on http://127.0.0.1 (never another interface) and the MCP endpoints builders report to and Helix works through.
It runs until you stop it (Ctrl-C). The loop runs on its own: either can restart without the other.

| Option | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--port <N>` | The port, instead of the config's app.port (47320 by default) |
| `--open` | Open it in the browser once it is up |
